novelty_risks: The core problem identified ('spectral over-counting of shared directions') was previously identified as 'merge interference from over-shared directions' in LoRA merging by Tang & Yang (2024).

The proposed solution (Singular Value Calibration) is mathematically and conceptually equivalent to Pico (Tang & Yang, 2024) applied to full-weight matrices via SVD rather than explicitly low-rank LoRA factors.
overlap_assessment: High conceptual overlap with Tang & Yang (2024). Both works identify that simple merging overemphasizes 'shared directions' (or 'spectral over-accumulation') in the output space (column-space left singular vectors in this paper, LoRA B matrices in Tang & Yang). Both works propose a data-free calibration step to downscale these over-represented components to restore balance.

relevant_prior_work.key_idea: Identifies that when merging multiple LoRA adapters, output-side matrices (B) tend to share a small set of directions. Naive merging overemphasizes these shared directions (merge interference), destroying task-specific information. Proposes Pico, a data-free method to identify over-shared directions, downscale them before merging, and rescale the final update.
relevant_prior_work.relation_to_submission: The submission discovers that shared knowledge aligns across tasks in spectral subspaces, causing 'spectral over-accumulation' and singular-value inflation, and fixes this by rescaling inflated singular values in column-space. This is conceptually identical to Tang & Yang's identification of 'over-shared directions' in LoRA B-matrices (which correspond to output/column space) and their calibration approach (Pico).
relevant_prior_work.source_evidence: Search result for 'shared directions improves performance combines prior work 2023 2024' describing Tang & Yang (2024).
relevant_prior_work.title: Crowded in B-Space: Calibrating Shared Directions for LoRA Merging
relevant_prior_work.why_it_matters_for_novelty: It preempts the submission's core theoretical contribution (the phenomenon of over-accumulating shared directions) and the essence of its solution (calibrating/downscaling those shared directions). The submission presents this as a novel discovery, but it was already presented at ICML 2024 for LoRA architectures.

relevant_prior_work.relation_to_submission: The submission cites TSV-M as a baseline. Both works use SVD to decompose task matrices and operate on the singular vector spaces to manage inter-task interference.

search_confidence: High. The search identified a highly relevant, un-cited prior work (Pico, ICML 2024) that directly anticipates the submission's core phenomenon and mitigation strategy.
strongest_novelty_defense: The submission extends the insight from explicitly low-rank, LoRA-specific architectures (where factors A and B are readily available) to general full-weight fine-tuning. It dynamically extracts the spectral subspaces via SVD and formulates a principled post-processing calibration (SVC) directly on the singular values.
